provenance.orgName: Wymondham, Norfolk. Benedictine abbey of Saint Mary the Virgin; originally priory and cell of St Albans
provenance.p: The calendar contains the dedication of the church (30 March). The ownership of the last prior of Tynemouth is marked (see below), but A. J. Horwood says 'The MS. seems to have been written at Wymondham Abbey'.

provenance.orgName: Tynemouth, Northumberland, Benedictine priory of St Mary the Virgin and St Oswin; cell of St Albans
provenance.p: Dompnus robertus Blakeney huius libri est possessor (flyleaf). Robert Blakeney was the last prior of Tynemouth.

history.provenance: Sir John Lawson, Brough Hall, Yorkshire. Compare Hist. MSS. Comm. Rep. 3 (1872) 255b. This was the last known provenance according to the first edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1941).

Dyson Perrins sale at Sotheby's, 11 April 1961, lot 123 to Quaritch. The manuscript was still intact at this stage, as noted in the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964), p. 191, n. 1.
Quaritch catalogue 820 (1961), no. 17. Still with Quartich in 1962 (£600).
Sold to Walter Schatzki, 153 East 57th Street, New York 22, who dismembered it before January 1963.

The 80 leaves that now constitute MS Lat. liturg. g.8 were acquired by the Bodleian in 1963 according to the catalogue entry in Medieval Manuscripts in Oxford Libraries (Typescript description by Bodleian library staff, revised by Peter Kidd, late 1990s). 'The remainder of this manuscript, a psalter and canticles on 226 leaves, s. xiv, has been dismembered, but photographs of the six pages with historiated initials are at the Bodleian' (Medieval Libraries of Great Britain, 2nd edn, p. 191, n. 1).

recordHist.source: Neil R. Ker, ed., Medieval Libraries of Great Britain: A List of Surviving Books, Royal Historical Society Guides and Handbooks, 3 (London, 1941; 2nd edn, 1964; supplement, ed. Andrew G. Watson, 1987; digital edn, ed. Richard Sharpe and James M. W. Willoughby, 2010–15).
